units.translation: But I will defend the suppliant and rescue him.
But I cannot help you without harm.
Help against the capture by enemies.
It helps to be silent and to learn my laws.
What help is there from mortals?

(with the first syllable of variable length, and indeed long at Sept. 135 244 344 469 910. Pers. 86. Suppl. 665. But it must be considered short where the meter either requires a short or admits either length. The genitive is "Αρεος or Αρεως, the accusative "Αρη, not "Αρην, which is sometimes introduced in copies. There are only two examples of the genitive in Aeschylus, "Αρεος Sept. 115 in the dochmiac verse "Αρεος ὀρόμενον, Αρεως ib. 64 at the beginning of a trimeter before a consonant, where in copies ἄρεος is found. On both cases see what I said in Lexicon Sophocleum p. 59 60. Ares is the god called Mars by the Latins. He is frequently named as the author of war or warlike tumult, discord and other evils, the name often being transferred to war itself, battle and slaughter.
[ἄρης [Ares] wrongly for ἀρῆς [curses] or ἀρᾶς [curses]: see under ἀρά [curse].]
